# ACL compression/decompression oracle

These fixtures were generated by the upstream MIT Animation Compression Library
**v2.1.0**, commit `414689d5cff4286a7898487a46dc5e48005d38da`, using its RTM
submodule at `d7982f2b2524feeb322f424b29cf43df30b5d5b7`. The `.acl` files are
outputs of the real upstream compressor. The matching `.csv` files contain every
stored sample independently read with the upstream C++ decompressor, using
nearest-sample rounding and rotation normalization. The first CSV row is
`track_count,frame_count,component_count,sample_rate`; remaining rows are frame
major samples. Components for QVV tracks are XYZW quaternion, XYZ translation,
and XYZ scale.

`oracle.cpp` is a development fixture generator. Cargo never compiles or links
it. The application and native decoder have no C++ or ACL runtime dependency.
The generator creates only deterministic synthetic animation, with no game data.
Upstream licenses are retained in `LICENSE-ACL` and `LICENSE-RTM`.

To reproduce, with an upstream v2.1.0 checkout (including the RTM submodule):

```sh
g++ -std=c++14 -O2 -I "$ACL_SRC/includes" -I "$ACL_SRC/external/rtm/includes" \
    oracle.cpp -o /tmp/assetstudio-acl-oracle
/tmp/assetstudio-acl-oracle .
```

The five scalar fixtures cover float1, float2, float3, float4, and vector4,
including constant values, quantized animated values, and raw animated fallback.
The seven QVV fixtures cover full precision, variable single/multiple segments,
six segments with local constant bit rates, raw fallback inside variable tracks,
multiple swizzled constant rotation groups, and wrap optimization. Rotations use
nonzero XYZ components; translations and scales have distinct components.

Rust tests compare every native decoded sample with the independent CSV values.
They also exercise repaired-hash truncations and deterministic payload mutations,
invalid section/count/bit-rate/range flags, and exact combined-allocation limits.

The verified native QVV scope is resident, unstripped ACL 2.1 data with trivial
default transforms, using full or dropped-W quaternions and full/variable vectors.
Database streaming, stripped keyframes, external default poses, development
versions 8/9, and engine-specific Tuanjie or customized game decoder maps require
separate verified implementations and return explicit errors where applicable.
